about: Trump Bill Signing shows Donald Trump seated at the Resolute Desk in the Oval Office, lips pressed together, holding up an open black folder toward the camera. The right page carries his jagged signature and the left page is blank, which made the photo an obvious canvas: people paste their own fake decree onto the paper, as if a president just made it law. The joke is the gap between the official ceremony and the petty, silly or overly specific "order" being displayed, like banning Monday meetings or making pizza a vegetable.
origin: The shot comes from the January 2017 signings of Trump's first executive orders, when he showed each signed document to the press pool. One of those was the order pulling the United States out of the Trans-Pacific Partnership trade deal.
usage:
This template has one text box, placed on the blank right-hand page of the folder. Write the decree as a short, official-sounding order: "effective immediately", "by executive order", "hereby banned". The funnier the contrast between bureaucratic phrasing and a trivial rule, the better.

It suits workplace wishes, house rules, fandom demands and hot takes stated as law. Keep it to one or two short lines so it fits the page and reads on a phone. Stay with the playful "I declare" angle rather than real political claims.
ideas: all meetings that could be an email are now illegal
pineapple on pizza is hereby banned
every dog must be petted on sight
the last slice belongs to whoever ordered
